neighbours.label: a group of people who have a condition or exposure (sufferers, patients, residents, pregnant women) as the subject, at the point where a verb of reporting or complaining of symptoms is expected ('sufferers have…', 'trekkers commonly…', 'the most frequent…'); output promotes ' report', ' reported', ' complaints'. Professionals as the subject in the same frame are quiet
fire: Hay fever sufferers often describe itchy eyes and a blocked nose.
Since the factory opened, nearby residents have had headaches and sore throats.
Patients on the new drug commonly mention dizziness in the first week.
Among night-shift nurses, the most frequent complaint is poor sleep.
People living with long Covid frequently say they feel exhausted by noon.
Divers who surface too fast have described joint pain and tingling skin.
Many women going through menopause experience hot flushes at night.
Office staff exposed to the fumes have felt nauseous and light-headed.

notes: Probes: 'sufferers have' 0.55, 'patients have' 0.62, 'sufferers frequently' 0.53, 'workers ... have' 0.49, 'most frequent complaints' 0.67; 'Neurologists frequently' 0.06, 'researchers have' 0.15.
